name: Plate Tectonics
statement: Earth's rigid outer shell is broken into moving plates, and the geology happens where they meet.
statementAccent: the geology happens where they meet
meaning: Plate tectonics is the theory that Earth's rigid outer shell, the lithosphere of crust and uppermost mantle, is broken into a set of large plates that move slowly over the hotter, weaker, ductile asthenosphere beneath. Most of Earth's major geological activity, its earthquakes, volcanoes, mountain-building, and the creation and destruction of ocean basins, is concentrated at the boundaries between plates rather than in their interiors. It is the unifying framework that ties these phenomena together, with the continents riding passively on plates that carry both continental and oceanic crust.
mechanism: Plates interact at three kinds of boundary. At divergent boundaries they move apart and new oceanic crust forms by seafloor spreading, as at the mid-ocean ridges. At convergent boundaries they move together, one plate subducting beneath another or two continents colliding to raise mountains. At transform boundaries they slide past each other, neither creating nor destroying crust. The motion is driven by the slow convection of the mantle, with slab pull, the sinking of cold, dense subducting slabs, now regarded as the dominant force, aided by ridge push, though the balance of driving forces remains debated.

examples.text: A divergent boundary where the American and Eurasian and African plates spread apart, creating new seafloor whose symmetric magnetic stripes confirmed spreading; Iceland sits astride it.
A convergent, continental-collision boundary where the Indian plate drives into Eurasia, raising the highest mountains on Earth, which are still rising.
A transform boundary where the Pacific and North American plates slide horizontally past each other, producing California's major earthquakes.

variants.name: Seafloor spreading and magnetic stripes
variants.text: Harry Hess's hypothesis that new crust forms at ridges, confirmed by the Vine-Matthews-Morley reading of symmetric magnetic stripes as a record of spreading and geomagnetic reversals.

variants.name: The Wilson cycle
variants.text: J. Tuzo Wilson's account of ocean basins opening and later closing, from his 1965 transform-fault work, later named for him, describing the long-term birth and death of oceans.

whyItMatters: Plate tectonics is the unifying theory of the earth sciences, the single framework that explains together the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes, the growth of mountain ranges, the opening and closing of ocean basins, the drift of continents, and long-term links to climate and the biogeography of life. It did for geology what evolution did for biology, replacing a collection of separate observations with one coherent, predictive theory, and it underlies everything from earthquake hazard assessment to the reconstruction of ancient Earth.

working.text: expect earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain-building to concentrate where plates meet, not in their stable interiors.
identify whether a boundary is divergent, convergent, or transform to predict whether crust is created, destroyed, or merely slid past.
treat the sinking of cold, dense subducting slabs as the main engine pulling plates along, with mantle convection as the setting.

limits: The ultimate driving forces are still debated, and the balance of slab pull, ridge push, and deeper mantle dynamics is not fully settled. Earth appears unique among the terrestrial planets in having active plate tectonics today, while Venus, Mars, and Mercury show single-plate, stagnant-lid behaviour, and when and how plate tectonics began on Earth is also debated. The deep-mantle picture, including plumes, slab behaviour in the lower mantle, and large low-velocity provinces, is still being refined, so the broad theory is secure even as its mechanisms are actively researched.
misreadings: Plates are not the same as continents: a plate is a slab of lithosphere that can carry both continental and oceanic crust, so the North American plate includes the continent plus much of the western Atlantic floor, and boundaries generally do not follow coastlines. Continental drift is not the same as plate tectonics: drift was Wegener's early, mechanism-less idea that continents plough through the oceans, while plate tectonics is the later, mechanism-supplied theory in which whole plates move and seafloor is created and destroyed.
origin: Synthesised in the mid-to-late 1960s from Alfred Wegener's continental drift (1912-1915), Arthur Holmes's mantle-convection idea, Harry Hess's seafloor spreading (1960-1962), the Vine-Matthews-Morley hypothesis (1963), and J. Tuzo Wilson's transform faults (1965).
